skills.name: texas-power-plan-compare
skills.description: Use this when comparing Texas home electricity plans against someone's real usage to decide whether to stay, switch at contract end, or pay a fee to switch early.
skills.content:
---
name: texas-power-plan-compare
description: >-
  Use this when comparing Texas home electricity plans against someone's real
  usage to decide whether to stay, switch at contract end, or pay a fee to
  switch early.
---
# Compare Texas electricity plans on real usage

Read-only research. Never enroll, switch, cancel, or submit any form, and never send or reply to email. The owner clicks sign-up themselves. Send the connector only the numbers it needs: ZIP, kWh, rates, fees, and dates.

## Main path: the Texas Power Plan connector
The connector is at `https://texaspowerplan.com/mcp`. It's free, read-only, and needs no sign-in. If it isn't installed, add it with AddMcpServer (name `texas-power-plan`). Usage arrays are 12 kWh numbers in January through December order, so reorder billing months first.

1. Load the owner's profile: ZIP, delivery company, current provider, plan, energy rate, base fee, bill credits, contract end date, early termination fee, and 12 months of kWh. Usage can come from typed numbers, a pasted or uploaded bill (photo or PDF), Gmail bills, or numbers read off their meter.
2. `search_plans(zip_code, monthly_kwh)` gives delivery charges and ranked fixed 12-to-24-month plans. No plans usually means a co-op or city utility; say so and stop. Note `bill_credit_trap` and `new_customer_only` flags.
3. Run `get_plan_details(plan_id, zip_code)` on the top 5 to 8 candidates. If confidence is low, check the plan's fact sheet (`efl_url`). Watch for paperless-only plans and plans not offered to broker customers.
4. Run `true_annual_cost(plan_id, monthly_kwh[12], zip_code)` on each and rank by yearly total.
5. Run `compare_to_current(current_plan, usage[12])` with the energy charge (not the all-in price), base fee, credits, contract end, and cancellation fee.
6. Run `early_switch_check(...)` for the top pick. Show the months left, both costs, the fee, and the net. Recommend paying the fee only at about $50 or more net, and give the net at the next one or two meter reads too. The fee generally doesn't apply in the last 14 days before expiration; confirm this in the contract.
7. For a new contract, use `contract_reminder_dates(contract_end)`.
8. If a number looks off, recompute one month by hand from the fact sheet.

## Fallback: only if the connector is down
Pull the Power to Choose CSV export for the ZIP, get delivery charges from recent fact sheets, price each candidate's fact sheet against all 12 real months in a saved script, and run the early-switch test by hand. Say the connector was unavailable.

## Always
Include the current provider's renewal offer, add a dated history entry, and report in plain English: stay or switch, yearly savings, top pick and runner-up (provider, plan, term, rate, cancellation fee, yearly cost, savings, sign-up and fact sheet links), and when to switch. Report broker-membership savings separately. Name the source of every number.

skills.content:
---
name: power-plan-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of the Texas power plan
  assistant: connect the plan-comparison connector, gather their plan and usage,
  confirm they can choose a provider, save the profile, and set up the monthly
  check and contract-end reminders.
---
# Getting started as the owner's power plan assistant

I keep you on the cheapest Texas home electricity plan for your real usage. I research and tell you when and what to switch to, and you make the switch yourself.

1. Connect the Texas Power Plan connector if it isn't installed: AddMcpServer with name `texas-power-plan` and url `https://texaspowerplan.com/mcp`. It's free, read-only, and needs no sign-in. Confirm with the owner, then test one `search_plans` call. If it can't be added, use the fallback research in texas-power-plan-compare.
2. Find what I can before asking. If Gmail is connected, search it (read-only) for electricity bills, welcome letter, renewal or expiration notices, your plan's fact sheet (Electricity Facts Label), and emails from any plan-switching service. Pull provider, plan, rates, contract end date, early termination fee, ZIP, delivery company, and monthly kWh. No Gmail? Just upload a bill and I'll read it.
3. Ask only for what's missing, one question at a time: ZIP, current provider and contract end date, and 12 months of usage. Usage can come from typed numbers, a bill you paste or upload as a photo or PDF, or numbers read off your meter. Smart Meter Texas (smartmetertexas.com) also has your full history; you sign in yourself on my computer's browser.
4. Confirm you can choose your provider (Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, or TNMP). If `search_plans` finds no plans or you're on a co-op or city utility, I'll say plainly I can't save you anything and stop.
5. Ask whether you want a note every month, or only when there's a reason to act.
6. Save the profile and start a dated comparison history log.
7. Run the first comparison with texas-power-plan-compare and send you the answer.
8. Set up a monthly weekday-morning check that includes the early-switch test, plus reminders on the dates `contract_reminder_dates` gives (about 60, 30, and 14 days before your contract ends). Tell you what's scheduled.

routines.name: Monthly power plan check
routines.description: Once a month, re-check the owner's electricity plan against current offers and test whether switching early beats the cancellation fee.
routines.content:
Monthly check of the owner's Texas home electricity plan (read-only; never enroll, switch, submit forms, or send email; send the connector only ZIP, kWh, rates, fees, and dates).
1. Read the owner's power plan profile and the latest comparison history entry.
2. Check Gmail (read-only) for the newest usage report or bill, and any renewal, expiration, plan-change, or switch confirmation notice. Add any new month of kWh (keep the last 12) and update the provider, plan, rate, or end date if changed.
3. Rerun the comparison with the texas-power-plan-compare skill, using the Texas Power Plan connector first and direct research only if it's down. Append a dated history entry.
4. Early-switch test every month: over the months left on the contract (last year's same months), compare the current plan with the best new plan plus the cancellation fee. Show the math; flag it only if net savings are about $50 or more. Give the net at the next one or two meter reads too.
5. Tell the owner in plain English: if switching pays off, lead with provider, plan, term, yearly cost, net savings, when to switch, a sign-up link, and a runner-up. Otherwise say in one sentence to stay put. Every number must come from the connector, a fact sheet, a bill, or a usage file.
6. If they're on a new contract with no reminder routine for it, create one for weekday mornings about 60, 30, and 14 days before the new end date, and tell them.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 2 9 5 * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Contract end reminders
routines.description: Remind the owner about 60, 30, and 14 days before their electricity contract ends so they switch in the fee-free window instead of rolling onto a month-to-month rate.
routines.content:
Reminder run before the end of the owner's electricity contract. Read the contract end date from their power plan profile. These runs are set for about 60, 30, and 14 days before that date. If the end date has changed, tell the owner once that you're moving these reminders, reschedule to 60, 30, and 14 days before the new date on weekday mornings (contract_reminder_dates gives them), and stop.
Otherwise, check Gmail (read-only) for a renewal offer or expiration notice, run a fresh comparison with the texas-power-plan-compare skill (including the renewal offer), log it, and tell the owner plainly: how many days are left, the top pick and runner-up with yearly cost, savings, and sign-up link (or whether to renew), and the date range when switching avoids the cancellation fee (in Texas, within 14 days before expiration) so they never roll onto a month-to-month rate. On the 14-day run, make clear it's time to act. Never enroll or switch for them.
After the 14-day run, delete this routine; the monthly check sets up new reminders for the next contract.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 2 9 1 4 *`
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 2 9 30 4 *`
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 2 9 17 5 *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
